title: session-load runs 1, 4 and 8 sessions at once and records what they cost together
goal: python3 _tools/benchmarks.py run session-load --sessions N,N... replays N sessions of each arm at once (default 1), each with its own session id and throwaway clone, and writes for N above 1 the same rows with case '<phase> <class> xN' and a load_peak row, the host's 1-minute load at its highest during the run

run:
import sys
def _fail(t, e, tb, _d=sys.excepthook):
    if issubclass(t, AssertionError):
        print('check failed:', e); sys.exit(1)
    _d(t, e, tb)
sys.excepthook = _fail
import csv, os, shutil, subprocess, tempfile
T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
B = os.path.join(T, 'bin'); os.mkdir(B)
open(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 'w').write('#!/bin/sh\nexit 1\n')
os.chmod(os.path.join(B, 'claude'), 0o755)
ENV = dict(os.environ, PATH=B + os.pathsep + os.environ['PATH'])
out = os.path.join(T, 'out.csv')
p = subprocess.run([sys.executable, '_tools/benchmarks.py', 'run', 'session-load', '--arms', 'A', '--sessions', '1,2', '--reps', '1', '--out', out],
                   capture_output=True, text=True, env=ENV, timeout=1800)
rows = list(csv.DictReader(open(out, encoding='utf-8'))) if os.path.exists(out) else []
shutil.rmtree(T, ignore_errors=True)
assert p.returncode == 0, ('run session-load --sessions 1,2 exit', p.returncode, p.stderr[-400:])
val = {(r['case'], r['arm'], r['metric']): float(r['value']) for r in rows if r['scenario'] == 'session-load'}
for case in ('idle all', 'working all'):
    one, two = val.get((case, 'A', 'cpu_s')), val.get((case + ' x2', 'A', 'cpu_s'))
    assert one is not None and two is not None, ('no 1-session or 2-session cpu_s row', case)
    assert two > one, ('2 sessions at once cost no more CPU than 1', case, one, two)
    assert (case + ' x2', 'A', 'load_peak') in val, ('no load_peak row for 2 sessions', case)

gates.question: How are the figures of N sessions that ran at once combined in a row with case xN?
options: sum over sessions, peak as the sum of peaks, wall_s the longest, hook timings pooled
sum, peak as the largest session's peak
gates.recommendation: sum over sessions, peak as the sum of peaks, wall_s the longest, hook timings pooled
gates.reason: the sum is what the host pays together, and a sum of peaks is the safe bound, noted on the row
gates.answer: sum over sessions, peak as the sum of peaks, wall_s the longest, hook timings pooled

gates.question: How is load_peak read and recorded?
options: case '<phase> all xN', polled every 0.5 s from the common start to the end of the sessions, median over the reps
once at the end of each run
the maximum over the reps rather than the median
gates.recommendation: case '<phase> all xN', polled every 0.5 s from the common start to the end of the sessions, median over the reps
gates.reason: the goal names the highest load during the run, and every other row is a median over the reps
gates.answer: case '<phase> all xN', polled every 0.5 s from the common start to the end of the sessions, median over the reps

gates.question: How do N sessions at once get their own clones and samplers?
options: one throwaway clone each (the first shared with the one-session rows), each replay with its own ps sampler paused N times as long, started together at a barrier
all sessions in one clone with separate session ids
one shared sampler across all sessions
gates.recommendation: one throwaway clone each (the first shared with the one-session rows), each replay with its own ps sampler paused N times as long, started together at a barrier
gates.reason: the goal asks for a throwaway clone per session, and the longer pause keeps the ps load constant
gates.answer: one throwaway clone each (the first shared with the one-session rows), each replay with its own ps sampler paused N times as long, started together at a barrier
